rags-to-riches.name: Rags to Riches
rags-to-riches.summary: Underdog journey from initial failure to eventual success. Pulls on resilience, grit, and perseverance — useful for founder stories, brand stories, and any deck where the audience needs to feel the cost behind the win.

beats.name: Origin
beats.description: Start at the bottom. Describe the humble beginning, the constraint, the moment before anything had been built. Concrete details — a place, a year, a feeling — earn the audience's investment in what follows.

beats.name: Inspiration
beats.description: Show the moment the protagonist found their calling. A conversation, a customer, a problem they couldn't unsee. The inspiration is the engine that pushes the rest of the story uphill.

beats.name: Opportunity
beats.description: Reveal the chance the protagonist took. Why this and not something safer? Make the choice visible — opportunities only count when there was something else they passed up to grab them.

beats.name: Adversity
beats.description: Walk through the hardest stretch. Concrete failures, near-misses, moments of doubt. Resist the temptation to skip past the pain — the audience trusts the win more when the loss was real.

beats.name: Overcoming
beats.description: Show how the obstacles got beaten. What changed, what was learned, what hard call was made. The transition from 'rags' to 'riches' should feel earned, not granted.

beats.name: Impactful Change
beats.description: Describe the moment the world tipped. The customer who said yes, the product that broke through, the metric that turned. One concrete transformation lands harder than a montage.

beats.name: Lasting Legacy
beats.description: Close on what the journey means for those who come next. The lesson, the people changed, the work that endures. Leave the audience with a takeaway that outlives the story.

sales.name: Sales
sales.summary: Sales team or prospective customers focused on product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI justification.
sales.description: Sales teams and prospective customers weighing product benefits, competitive differentiation, and ROI. Put customer success stories first, back claims with visual proof points, state the value proposition plainly, and close on a strong call to action. Moderate chart density; 15-25 slides.

inform.name: Inform
inform.summary: Give the audience clear context, facts, or status without asking for a decision.
inform.description: Use when the deck needs to make the audience aware of current state, background, or findings. Prioritize clarity, completeness, and accurate framing over persuasion.
inform.outcome: The audience understands the situation and can repeat the important facts.
successCriteria: Audience can summarize the key facts
Follow-up questions are about implications, not basic context

conversational.name: Conversational
conversational.summary: Direct, dialog-style voice for podcasts, fireside chats, and small-group reviews.
conversational.description: Sound like one half of a real conversation. Ask questions on the slide and answer them; keep paragraphs short; lean into examples over abstractions. Useful when the deck is meant to support a discussion rather than to lecture.
voiceCues: Ask a question on the slide, then answer it on the next.
Use second person — speak to the room, not at it.
Lean on stories and concrete examples over abstract framing.
Keep each idea to one short paragraph; let the dialog do the rest.
avoid: Stuffing slides — leave room for the discussion.
Inside-baseball references the room may not share.
samplePhrases: Why now? Two things changed in the last six months.
Here's the part that surprised us — and what we did about it.
If you take one thing from this section, take this.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

boost.name: Boost
boost.summary: High-energy digital accents for demos and launch moments.
boost.description: A vivid blue-red digital palette with bright chart accents. Best for product stories that need strong on-screen presence.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

meiryo.name: Meiryo
meiryo.textSample: これはメイリオフォントで書かれています
meiryo.description: Meiryo is a sans serif OPF font scheme for East Asian presentations, using Meiryo for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
